presidents.name: George H. W. Bush
trivia: First sitting vice president elected president since Martin Van Buren in 1836.
Youngest pilot in the U.S. Navy when he earned his wings in World War II; he was shot down in the Pacific and rescued.
Before the presidency he was CIA director, UN ambassador, U.S. envoy to China, and Reagan’s vice president.
Built a large international coalition and drove Iraqi forces from Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War.
Broke his 1988 pledge “Read my lips: no new taxes,” which damaged him in the 1992 campaign.
Father of George W. Bush—the second father-son presidential pair after John and John Quincy Adams.
During a 1992 debate he checked his watch on camera, a moment critics said made him look bored or out of touch.
Lost reelection in a three-way race against Bill Clinton and independent Ross Perot.
Celebrated birthdays with parachute jumps even as a former president in his 80s and 90s.
Captained Yale’s baseball team and later made his fortune in the Texas oil business.
Pub-trivia shorthand: Reagan’s VP; Gulf War; “read my lips”; dad of George W. Bush.

presidents.name: Bill Clinton
trivia: First Baby Boomer generation president (born 1946).
First president to send an email from the White House, and the first to oversee an official White House website.
Second president impeached by the House (over lying about the Monica Lewinsky affair); the Senate acquitted him.
Presided over the long 1990s economic expansion and federal budget surpluses near the end of his term.
Rhodes Scholar who studied at Oxford, earned a Yale Law degree, and was Arkansas governor before the White House.
Signed NAFTA and the 1996 welfare reform law that replaced Aid to Families with Dependent Children with Temporary Assistance for Needy Families.
Played saxophone on Arsenio Hall’s late-night show in 1992, a campaign moment that made him look younger and cooler than rivals.
Told the nation, “I did not have sexual relations with that woman, Miss Lewinsky”—a denial later undercut by evidence.
Wife Hillary Clinton later served as U.S. senator from New York, secretary of state, and the 2016 Democratic presidential nominee.
Born in Hope, Arkansas, and nicknamed “Bubba” by friends and Southern supporters.
Pub-trivia shorthand: 1990s boom / sax-on-Arsenio / impeached over Lewinsky; Hillary’s husband.

presidents.name: George W. Bush
trivia: Only president with a Master of Business Administration degree (Harvard Business School).
President during the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks; ordered the invasion of Afghanistan and, in 2003, Iraq.
Created the Department of Homeland Security and signed the USA PATRIOT Act expanding surveillance powers.
Won the 2000 election after the Supreme Court’s Bush v. Gore decision halted Florida’s recount.
Owned a share of the Texas Rangers MLB franchise and helped get their new ballpark built before becoming governor.
Nickname “Dubya” comes from the Texas pronunciation of his middle initial W.
Three days after 9/11 he stood on World Trade Center rubble with a bullhorn and told rescue workers, “I can hear you… the rest of the world hears you.”
Yale and Harvard educated, but campaigned as a plain-spoken Texas governor.
Twin daughters Barbara and Jenna were often in celebrity news during his presidency.
Son of President George H. W. Bush—the modern father-son presidential pair.
Pub-trivia shorthand: 9/11 president; Afghanistan and Iraq; Bush v. Gore; “Dubya.”

presidents.name: Barack Obama
trivia: First African American president of the United States.
First president born outside the contiguous 48 states (Honolulu, Hawaii).
Signed the Affordable Care Act (2010), the health-insurance overhaul nicknamed “Obamacare.”
Ordered the 2011 Navy SEAL raid in Pakistan that killed al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden.
Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2009, less than a year into his first term.
Won in 2008 on the slogan “Yes We Can” and a message of hope and change after the financial crisis.
Worked as a Chicago community organizer and taught constitutional law at the University of Chicago before the U.S. Senate.
Married to Michelle Obama; daughters Malia and Sasha spent their childhoods in the White House.
Known for regular White House basketball games with staff and friends.
Defeated John McCain in 2008 and Mitt Romney in 2012.
Pub-trivia shorthand: first Black president; Obamacare; bin Laden raid; born in Hawaii.

presidents.name: Donald Trump
trivia: First president with no prior military service and no prior elected office.
First president impeached twice by the House (2019 and 2021); the Senate acquitted him both times.
Appointed three Supreme Court justices in one term: Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett.
Brokered the Abraham Accords, normalizing relations between Israel and several Arab states including the UAE and Bahrain.
Later won a second, nonconsecutive term as president #47—only the second person after Grover Cleveland to do so.
Became nationally famous as a New York real-estate developer and host of the NBC reality show The Apprentice.
Ran on the slogan “Make America Great Again,” shortened to MAGA on hats and signs.
Recognized Jerusalem as Israel’s capital and moved the U.S. embassy there from Tel Aviv.
Lost the 2020 election to Joe Biden and falsely claimed the election was stolen.
Born in Queens, New York City—like Theodore Roosevelt, a president born in NYC.
Pub-trivia shorthand: celebrity outsider; MAGA; impeached twice; comes back later as #47.

presidents.name: Joe Biden
trivia: Oldest person ever inaugurated as president (age 78 in 2021).
First president from Delaware.
Longest-serving U.S. senator to become president (36 years representing Delaware).
Signed the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and the Inflation Reduction Act on climate and health costs.
Completed the U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan in 2021, ending America’s longest war.
Served as Barack Obama’s vice president from 2009 to 2017.
For decades he took Amtrak home to Wilmington most nights instead of living full-time in Washington.
Survived surgery for two brain aneurysms in 1988 and returned to the Senate.
Ended his 2024 reelection bid after a poor debate performance and endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris.
First sitting vice president elected president since George H. W. Bush in 1988.
Pub-trivia shorthand: Obama’s VP; oldest inaugurated president; ends the Afghanistan war; Amtrak Joe.

presidents.name: Donald Trump
trivia: Second president to serve nonconsecutive terms (after Grover Cleveland); he is the same person as president #45.
Oldest person ever elected president (age 78 at the 2024 election).
First former president since Cleveland to lose a reelection bid and then win the presidency again later.
Survived an assassination attempt at a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, in July 2024.
Defeated Kamala Harris in 2024 with running mate J.D. Vance as vice president.
In 2024 he became the first former president convicted of felonies (a New York hush-money case), then won the presidency anyway.
Only president other than Cleveland whose two terms have different official numbers.
His 2024 campaign was widely framed as a comeback rematch after losing in 2020.
Quiz questions often ask why the United States can have both a 45th and 47th president who are the same person.
Began his second term in January 2025.
Pub-trivia shorthand: Trump’s second, nonconsecutive term—same person as #45; Cleveland comparison.
